graph.mif is a Quartus MIF: 32-bit words, depth 10,124, with unused memory zero-filled. Use your project’s MIF ROM wrapper. Padded HEX is for $readmemh simulation; regular HEX can be re-imported here.

How your FPGA uses this file

Compile your design for up to 100 nodes. Read the active node count and neighbour count from the header to control Dijkstra’s loops.

Read the connection block for destinations and weights. Read the coordinate block to position the nodes and draw their connections through your VGA renderer.

Metadata cannot change compiled signal widths. Updating a ROM initialization file needs a memory-image or bitstream update; live loading needs a RAM loader.

The exported coordinates match your node centres. VGA drawing logic still supplies the circles, labels, directed lines and weight text.
NodeForge0-based nodes · Directed edges · Integer weights 0–255Built for the path ahead.

Table → graph → MIF.

  1. Set 1–100 nodes and 1–100 neighbour slots, then press Apply.
  2. Enter destination (weight), for example 4 (12). Node IDs and weights are decimal. A blank slot has no edge.
  3. Paste a range from Excel. Reverse edges must be entered separately. Zero weights, self-loops and parallel edges are supported.
  4. Drag nodes or enter their X/Y position. The graph uses a 640 × 480 pixel canvas. These positions become the VGA coordinates.
  5. Optionally run Dijkstra to check the connections.
  6. Click Generate MIF. The downloaded graph.mif contains metadata, weighted connections and coordinates, in that order.
Both formats contain the same NFG1 memory image. MIF adds Quartus headers, addresses and zero padding. Your existing 12-bit ROM reader must be adapted once to its memory map. Hardware widths stay fixed; the header selects the active graph size.

Original ROM imports use the selected node/slot counts. NFG1 imports restore counts and node positions automatically.

Edits stay in this page. For an editable backup, download regular HEX before closing this page; importing that HEX restores the table and layout. MIF and padded HEX are FPGA exports.
